text:
anya: Quick FYI — ran a tiny canary for raven-lite int4 on the funcall /structured-output suite. Seeing a small but reproducible class of failures: duplicated tool invocations + truncated JSON suffixes when the model outputs close near token boundaries.

raj: I reproduced. Replays show identical prompt + no invocation-id header -> backend sees two in-flight requests after retry loop flips. Suspect retry/backoff tweak we rolled last week exposed a race.

olivia: numbers? how bad is truncated JSON vs duplicate calls?

anya: summary from the canary (1000 invokes):
- baseline float32 run: parse-pass 98.7%
- int8 run: parse-pass 97.9%
- int4 canary: parse-pass 94.1%
- duplicate tool invoke rate (int4): 2.3% (zero in baseline)
- truncated-suffix smell: ~1.6% (mostly suffix cut at closing brace or trailing array element)

raj: sample log snippets show missing invocation metadata:
```
2026-02-12T18:02:01Z handler: start request id=abc123 prompt=... invocation-id=null
2026-02-12T18:02:01Z runtime: spawned invoke tool `search` -> tool-run-id=tr-9x
2026-02-12T18:02:01Z handler: retrying request (backoff) id=abc123 -> new attempt created without carryover invocation-id
2026-02-12T18:02:02Z runtime: spawned invoke tool `search` -> tool-run-id=tr-9y
```

mike: so two tool runs for same logical request. That explains duplicates. Truncated JSON probably unrelated?

anya: they correlate. When the model emits right at the token boundary the streamer cut/merge + us reissuing a second attempt can produce partial+partial -> merged truncation or extra suffix.

olivia: low-hanging mitigation?

raj: immediate 2-step plan: 1) dedupe at proxy/handler by honoring X-Invocation-Id header and ignoring duplicate logical ids for N seconds; 2) add a postprocess "closing-brace heal" in the structured-output sanitizer that attempts minimal fixes (append missing ']' or '}' and reparse) for canary-only.

anya: small patch I sketched to inject invocation id from SDK if missing:
```
# pseudo
invoc = headers.get('X-Invocation-Id') or gen_uuid()
handler.ctx.invocation_id = invoc
# downstream: runtime checks handler.ctx.invocation_id and de-dupes
```

mike: sdk change ETA? we should also guard server-side so older SDKs don't get harmed.

raj: server-side guard first, SDK followup. I'll spin a proxy hotfix branch that ignores duplicate invocations for 5s and returns 409 for replays (so clients get deterministic failure).

canary-bot: canary run updated: int4-run-2 started at 1761112280, routing 1% traffic to canary branch with de-dupe proxy.

evaluator-bot: quick after-patch snapshot (500 invokes): parse-pass 95.8%, duplicate rate 0.1%, truncated-suffix 0.6%. Improvement but still lower than int8.

anya: good progress. next: run a longer ensemble canary with streaming enabled + kv-cache disabled to isolate tokenizer boundary effects. Also add a test that forces rapid retry to ensure dedupe holds.

olivia: I'll add alerting for duplicate-tool-invoke >=0.5% and a dashboard for invocation-id coverage by SDK version.

mike: agree. rollout plan: ship proxy hotfix -> run 24h canary at 5% -> sdk patch follows next week -> if stable promote. If parse-pass doesn't hit >=97% at 5% we rollback.

raj: I'll open PR now for proxy dedupe + simple memcache for seen invocation ids (ttl 10s). tagging @anya for sanitizer patch.

anya: thanks — will open sanitizer PR and include the small JSON-close heuristics behind a canary flag.

olivia: logging note: include invocation-id in downstream tool logs and in structured-output telemetry so we can trace tool-run-id -> invocation-id.

mike: sweet. ping here when PRs are up and when the 24h canary starts. :thumbsup:
